answer: Identity verification uses a challenge-bound sequence of modular squarings, where each result depends on the previous one. GPUs may compute separate clone sequences concurrently, but cannot parallelize the steps of any single sequence to evade its required elapsed time; every clone therefore incurs a physical delay. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the completed work efficiently, while lotus, thread, and river provide distinct identity labels, not shortcuts around the sequential cost.
